# legal

Generates a **Privacy Policy** + **Terms & Conditions** for an app from its data-use profile.
Deterministic template filling — **not legal advice**. Every document is stamped *"requires
human/legal review before publishing"* and `generate()` returns `review_required=True`.

Why it exists: the App Store **requires a privacy policy** (Guideline 5.1). The compliance agent
only *checks* for one; this produces a truthful first draft grounded in what the app actually does
— especially **on-device** processing (no server → strong, honest privacy stance).

```python
from legal import AppLegalProfile, write_legal_docs

profile = AppLegalProfile(
    app_name="Color Matching", company="EIK Tech", contact_email="privacy@eiktech.co",
    collects_data=["a selfie you take (processed on-device)"], on_device=True,
    uses_iap=True, region="France", effective_date="2026-07-02",
)
res = write_legal_docs(profile, "apps/color-matching/legal")
res["review_required"]   # True — always
res["warnings"]          # e.g. unfilled placeholders + the mandatory lawyer-review note
```

Placeholders left as `[COMPANY]`, `[JURISDICTION]`, etc. are surfaced in `warnings` so nothing
ships half-filled. **A lawyer must review the output before it goes live.**
